title: why five times
hookLine: why five times; standing, bowing, forehead to the ground
last: THE FIVE PILLARS — A HOUSE BUILT ON FIVE.

cards: Ten past one on a weekday, in the stockroom behind a hardware store. One of the staff flattens a clean cardboard box on the floor, turns to face a particular direction, and stands very still.

Then he bows, hands on his knees. Then he goes all the way down, forehead to the cardboard, between the paint cans and the delivery crates. A few minutes later he folds the box away and goes back to the register.
Why five times a day? And why the whole body?

teach.h: SALAT — A SET SHAPE, AT SET TIMES.
teach.b: Salat. It's the second pillar, and it isn't quite what English means by prayer. Du'a is asking, in your own words, any time.
Salat is a set shape, at set times, with set words. The Qur'an says: “Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity.” The five times follow the sun.
Fajr before sunrise. Dhuhr after midday. Asr in the afternoon.
Maghrib just after sunset. Isha at night. Where does five come from?
A saying of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tells it. On the Night Journey he was given fifty daily prayers.

On the way back, Musa, Moses, asked what he'd been given, and said: your people can't manage that; go back and ask for less. He went back, again and again, until it was five. And God said: five, with the reward of fifty.
Many pray them at five separate times; Shia practice also allows joining them into three sittings, and the prayers are still five. Now the body.
Each prayer is made of units called rak'ahs, and each moves through the same shapes. Standing, and reciting al-Fatiha, the seven verses from day two. Bowing, back flat, hands on the knees.
Then sujud: forehead, nose, palms, knees and toes on the ground. Another saying tells that a person is never nearer to God than there.
The part of you that thinks, set down where your feet were.

how: Muslims pray salat five times a day, facing Mecca, in a set sequence of standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting; they may pray at home, at work, at a mosque, or anywhere clean.

games.q: what's inside the prayer — tap the pairs.
p: forehead, nose, palms, knees, toes down

s: salat and du'a are the same thing
du'a is asking in your own words, any time. salat is the set prayer, at set times, in a set shape.
in the hadith, the first number given was fifty
fifty, then five, after Musa sent the Prophet back to ask for less. five, with the reward of fifty.
all Muslims pray the five prayers at five separate times
Shia practice allows joining them into three sittings; the prayers are still five.

games.q: on the Night Journey, the Prophet ﷺ is given fifty daily prayers. on the way back, Musa stops him: your people can't manage that. what does he do?
o: go back and ask for fewer.
games.why: he went back, again and again, until it was five, and God said: five, with the reward of fifty.

practice: If you're able, stand for a moment, then bow a little, hands on your knees, and notice how your breath changes in each shape.
If you'd rather stay seated, lower your head toward your chest, slowly, and feel what the body says when it bows. Stay there, and let the body do the praying for once, without any words.

wordCard.voice: Salat. The prayer in its set shape: five times a day, standing, bowing, forehead to the ground. Tenth word.

orig.note: Arabic: the set prayer, the second pillar. often spoken as salah.

carryVoice: Your line: the body prays too. And if you prayed for a while and then stopped, you're in plenty of company: many come back one prayer at a time. Day ten.

sources.q: Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity
